_note: Plan D20 / WP4: every value needs a cited source that someone read; none is invented. method picks the heat series in src/pollination/engine/phenology.py; heat_threshold is the heat sum at threshold_stage; the window ends at heat_bloom_end if set, else after bloom_days (centred on the threshold day for full_bloom). uncertainty_days is the RMSE the source reports. All models run on NASA POWER daily T2M_MAX/T2M_MIN with Tmean = (Tmax + Tmin) / 2. Checks against observed bloom dates are in issue #35.

apple.source: Chmielewski F-M, Blümel K, Henniges Y, Blanke M, Weber RWS, Zoth M (2011) Phenological models for the beginning of apple blossom in Germany. Meteorol Z 20:487-496, doi:10.1127/0941-2948/2011/0258; bloom length: Sepsi P (2016) PhD thesis, Szent István University, doi:10.14751/SZIE.2016.047
apple.note: Beginning of bloom (BBCH 61), model M1: sigmoid forcing (Eq. 3.2) from t1 = 1 January, TBf = 3.3 °C, F* = 143 FU, RMSE 4.28 days (Table 2, Germany). Bloom length 15 days: mean from first flower to end of petal fall, n = 2426, Sepsi 2016 p. 72 and Table 25. Fitted on station daily means; POWER (Tmax + Tmin) / 2 is used instead.

sour_cherry.source: Matzneller P, Blümel K, Chmielewski F-M (2014) Models for the beginning of sour cherry blossom. Int J Biometeorol 58:703-715, doi:10.1007/s00484-013-0651-1; bloom end calibrated on Szabó T (2007) PhD thesis, Corvinus University of Budapest, Annex 7
sour_cherry.status: sourced; heat_bloom_end calibrated by the team on cited observations
sour_cherry.note: Beginning of bloom (BBCH 60), model M1: linear GDD from t1 = 1 March (DOY 60), TBF = 2.0 °C, F* = 250.7 (Table 4; RMSE 4.30 days on validation). heat_bloom_end: median GDD (same base and start) at the observed end of bloom of 'Újfehértói fürtös', 1983-2005 (Szabó 2007, Annex 7), computed on NASA POWER; leave-one-year-out RMSE 3.1 days. On the same data the start threshold has RMSE 3.8 days.

sunflower.status: no bloom model: the grower's declared window is used, NDYI is shown as evidence
leads: NDSU sunflower GDD model quoted at base 6.7 C, R1 569 / R5.1 883 GDD, in a Manitoba sheet that is now a 404 (https://residents.manitoba.ca/agriculture/crops/crop-management/pubs/frost-sunflowers.pdf); unverified, start point (sowing or emergence) unknown
sunflower.note: No NDYI bloom threshold is set, on purpose. On the cached HLS series of the five demo parcels (2022 and 2024) the weekly NDYI rises with the green canopy as well as with the flowers: a peak-and-half-height rule gave a 2 to 3 week bloom around the turn of June and July on four parcels in 2024, but 5 to 10 week plateaus on the others, and two parcels carried a spring crop in 2022. A threshold needs fields with a known crop and observed bloom dates; until then the bloom state is the declared window (Reported) and NDYI is displayed next to it.

black_locust.source: Kim S, Kim TK, Yoon S, et al. (2021) J Korean Soc For Sci 110(3):322-340, doi:10.14578/jkfs.2021.110.3.322 (chill-days model of Cesaraccio et al. 2004, doi:10.1016/j.agrformet.2004.03.002); bloom length: Ábri T, Keserű Z, Rédei K (2022) Erdészettudományi Közlemények 12:31-42, doi:10.17164/EK.2022.02
black_locust.note: Full bloom: chill days from 1 October of the previous year to C* = -138.95 °D, then forcing to F* = 247.73 °D, TB = 8.88 °C (single national model, p. 327; equations Table 2; validation RMSE 6.11 days, Table 4). Fitted on Korean data. Bloom length 10 days, the middle of 8-12 days for the 'Nyírségi' cultivar (Ábri et al. 2022, p. 33, citing Keresztesi 1984), centred on full bloom.
